Soften the onions, garlic and peppers in the oil, add the crushed tomatoes and reduce for 20 minutes.
Moisten with the stock and white wine, add the Espelette pepper and crumbled stale bread; thicken for 15 minutes.
Poach the hake sections for 8 minutes in this broth, without letting it boil.
Add the mussels and prawns, cover for 4 minutes until the shells open, and cover with parsley.

gateau-basque.d: A thick shortcrust enclosing either pastry cream or black cherry jam from Itxassou. The two camps do not agree, and every village holds its own version to be the only authentic one.
s: Cream the softened butter with 200 g of sugar, add two eggs, then the flour, ground almonds and baking powder.
Bring together without kneading, wrap and rest for 3 hours in the fridge: this dough is soft and only handles well when cold.
Make a pastry cream with the milk, yolks, remaining sugar and cornstarch; flavour with rum and cool it.
Line a deep tin with two thirds of the dough and fill with the cream — or cherry jam — stopping short of the edge.
Cover with the remaining dough, seal, glaze with egg and score with a fork. Bake for 40 minutes at 180°C.

tourtiere-landaise.d: Sheets of dough stretched by hand until translucent, buttered, crumpled and piled over apples in armagnac. Cut into, it collapses into a thousand shards — the sign of a successful one.
s: Knead flour, warm water, oil and salt for 20 minutes into a very elastic dough; oil it and rest for 2 hours.
Fry the sliced apples with 100 g of sugar, flame with armagnac and let them cool.
Stretch the dough by hand over a large floured cloth, working from the centre, until you can see the weave through it.
Brush generously with melted butter and cut into wide squares.
Layer crumpled pastry and apples in a tin, finish with three crumpled layers, sugar them and bake for 30 minutes at 190°C.

millas.d: A maize porridge set in a slab, cut into diamonds and fried in butter, sugared as it comes out. Savoury, it accompanied confit; sweetened, it became the after-school treat of the South-West.
s: Bring the milk, water, zest and a pinch of salt to a simmer.
Rain in the cornmeal, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Stir with a wooden spoon for 40 minutes over low heat: the mass should pull away from the sides.
Off the heat, work in the eggs, 50 g of butter and the orange blossom water, then spread 2 cm deep in a dampened dish. Set overnight.
Cut into diamonds, fry them in salted butter 4 minutes a side and sugar them generously as they leave the pan.

gardiane-de-taureau.d: Camargue bull meat stewed in red wine with black olives and orange peel, served over Camargue rice. The dish of the gardians, the mounted herdsmen of the delta marshes.
s: Marinate the meat in large cubes for 24 hours in the red wine with the vegetables, orange peel and aromatics.
Drain, dry thoroughly, then sear the meat in very hot oil, in small batches.
Fry the lardons and the marinade vegetables, then dust with flour.
Pour in the marinade brought to the boil, add the juniper, and simmer for 3 hours over very low heat.
Add the stoned olives for the last half hour. Serve over plain Camargue rice.

petits-pates-de-pezenas.d: Small cylinders of pastry filled with mutton and sugar, sweet and savoury like a medieval recipe. They are said to come from the Indian cooks of Lord Clive of India, who stayed at Pézenas in 1768.
s: Rub the cold butter into the flour, bind with an egg and a little iced water, and chill for an hour.
Chop the mutton and fat by knife into small dice, then mix with the brown sugar, zest, spices and rum.
Rest the filling overnight: the sugar must dissolve into it completely.
Cut strips of pastry, form small cylinders 5 cm high, fill them and close with a pleated disc of dough.
Glaze with egg and bake for 35 minutes at 190°C. Eaten warm, never scalding.

bourride.d: The white sister of bouillabaisse: the fish broth is bound with aioli off the heat until it becomes a silky cream. The whole difficulty is there — one degree too hot and the sauce splits.
s: Make a stock with the trimmings, leek, fennel, onion, white wine and orange peel for 25 minutes; strain it.
Mount an aioli in a mortar: garlic crushed with salt, three yolks, then oil in a thread until firm.
Poach the fish sections for 10 minutes in the simmering stock, then lift them out and keep them warm.
Slacken half the aioli with two yolks, then pour a ladle of hot stock over it, whisking.
Return everything to the pan off the heat and stir constantly until it thickens, never exceeding 80°C.

pieds-et-paquets.d: Lamb tripe stuffed with bacon and garlic, tied into small parcels and stewed for eight hours with sheep's trotters. A dish of absolute patience, prepared the day before for Sunday.
s: Blanch the tripe for 15 minutes, rinse it and cut it into 10 cm squares.
Mix the chopped bacon, garlic and parsley; place a spoonful on each square and fold into a parcel.
Fasten each parcel by cutting a slit in the tripe and threading the opposite corner through — never string, tradition forbids it.
Pack the parcels and trotters tightly in a pot with onion, carrot, tomato, white wine, zest and aromatics.
Cover with water, bring to a bare simmer and cook for 8 hours at 120°C. Serve the next day, reheated.

tourte-de-blettes.d: A sweet pie of chard leaves, apple, pine nuts and raisins. The vegetable vanishes under the sugar and leaves only a green freshness: nobody guesses, and that is the whole point.
s: Rub together the flour, butter and 80 g of sugar, bind with an egg and rest for an hour in the fridge.
Strip the ribs from the chard and keep only the green; shred it finely and salt it for 20 minutes to draw out water.
Squeeze it dry by the handful, then mix with the grated apple, pine nuts, rum-soaked raisins, remaining sugar, zest and parmesan.
Line a tin, fill it, cover with a lid of pastry and seal the edges by crimping.
Bake for 45 minutes at 180°C, cool completely and dust with icing sugar. Eaten cold.

crozets-au-beaufort.d: Tiny squares of buckwheat pasta, baked under beaufort with local sausage. The name comes from the Savoyard croé, cross: they were once cut one by one with a knife on the farmhouse table.
s: Knead the flours and eggs into a hard dough, rest it for an hour, then roll it very thin.
Cut 5 mm squares — it takes time, but that is what makes a crozet.
Fry the lardons and onions in the butter, deglaze with white wine and reduce.
Cook the crozets for 12 minutes in boiling salted water: they stay firm.
Toss everything with the cream and two thirds of the beaufort, tip into a dish, cover with the rest and brown for 15 minutes at 200°C.

farcon-savoyard.d: A cake of grated potato, prunes and bacon, cooked for four hours in a bain-marie in a mould lined with bacon. Sweet and savoury, it went to the village oven in the morning and came back for supper.
s: Grate the raw potatoes finely and squeeze them in a cloth: the water would ruin the texture.
Mix with the eggs, cream, sugar, spices, stoned prunes, raisins and diced pears.
Line a charlotte mould with bacon rashers, letting them hang over the sides.
Fill it, fold the rashers over the top and cover with buttered paper and a lid.
Cook for 4 hours in a bain-marie at 150°C. Let it settle for 20 minutes before turning out and slicing.

bacalhau-com-natas.d: Flaked salt cod and matchstick fried potatoes bound with béchamel and cream, browned in the oven. Said to be the most ordered restaurant dish in Portugal — and certainly the most consoling.
s: Desalt the cod for 36 hours, changing the water six times, then poach it for 8 minutes in the milk with the bay; flake it and keep the milk.
Cut the potatoes into matchsticks and fry them until barely golden: they will finish cooking in the oven.
Soften the onion and garlic in the olive oil, add the flaked cod and let it take up the flavour.
Make a béchamel with the butter, flour and infused milk, then loosen it with the cream and season with nutmeg.
Combine cod, potatoes and sauce, tip into a dish and bake for 25 minutes at 200°C.

carne-vinha-d-alhos.d: Pork marinated for a week in wine and garlic, then fried and served in a bolo do caco. Portuguese navigators carried this marinade as far as Goa, where it became vindaloo.
s: Cut the pork into 4 cm cubes and put them in a jar with the wine, vinegar, crushed garlic, bay, thyme and chilli.
Marinate for five to seven days in the cold, stirring daily: the meat should pale and tenderise.
Drain and dry thoroughly, then fry the cubes in lard until well coloured.
Pour a glass of strained marinade into the pan and reduce to a glaze, coating the meat.
Serve with orange slices, roast sweet potato and warm bolo do caco.

bolo-de-mel.d: The Madeiran Christmas cake, made with cane honey and thirteen spices, prepared on 8 December and broken only by hand — never cut. It keeps for a year and improves with age.
s: Warm the cane honey with the butter and lard until melted, then let it cool a little.
Pound the cinnamon, cloves, fennel and star anise in a mortar and mix them into the flour with the bicarbonate.
Work in the warm honey, sugar, rum and zest, and knead for 10 minutes: the dough is heavy and sticky.
Add the candied fruit, chopped walnuts and almonds, then rest the dough for three days in the cold, covered.
Divide between shallow round tins and bake for 50 minutes at 170°C. Wait three weeks before touching it.

arroz-de-tamboril.d: A monkfish rice served loose in an earthenware dish, with prawns and coriander. In Portugal a fish rice must be malandrinho — badly behaved, they say: it must on no account hold together.
s: Make a stock with the monkfish head and backbone for 25 minutes, then strain it.
Make a refogado: onion, garlic and pepper softened slowly in oil, then grated tomato cooked down.
Pour in the white wine, let it evaporate, add the rice and toast it for two minutes.
Moisten with boiling stock — three times the volume of rice, the dish must stay very wet — and cook for 12 minutes.
Add the monkfish in large medallions and the prawns for 6 minutes, then cut the heat and cover with chopped coriander.

caldeirada-de-enguias.d: Eels from the Ria de Aveiro stewed in layers with potatoes, onions and peppers. The moliceiro fishermen — whose sailing boats harvested seaweed — cooked it on board in a cast-iron pot.
s: Have the eels cut into 6 cm sections and let them draw with coarse salt for 30 minutes, then rinse them.
Cut all the vegetables into even 5 mm rounds.
Build the pot in layers: onion, potato, pepper, tomato, eel, salting and oiling each storey.
Repeat, finish with vegetables, pour in the white wine and water to come only halfway, and add paprika, chilli and bay.
Simmer for 35 minutes without stirring — shake the pot instead — and cover with coriander. Serve with firm polenta.

pao-de-lo-de-ovar.d: An egg cake deliberately underbaked, its heart left runny as custard. It is baked in a paper-lined mould, and success is judged by the wobble of the centre as it leaves the oven.
s: Line a round mould with baking paper, letting it overhang generously, without buttering it.
Whisk the yolks, whole eggs and sugar over a warm bain-marie for 15 minutes: the mixture should treble and pale.
Take it off the heat and keep whisking until completely cold.
Fold in the sifted flour in three additions, lifting with a spatula and never knocking out the air.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes at 180°C. The rim should be set and the centre still liquid: take it out before you feel reassured.

sopa-de-peixe-algarvia.d: A rockfish soup thickened with bread, scented with coriander and chilli. Olhão, a port of tuna boats and canneries, has made it its everyday soup since the town began.
s: Cook the rockfish for 25 minutes in two litres of water with the bay, then pass the broth through a food mill.
Soften the onion, garlic and pepper in the oil, add the grated tomato and reduce for 20 minutes.
Pour in the strained broth and white wine, add the chilli and simmer for 10 minutes.
Crumble the stale bread into the soup, let it swell, then crush it with a wooden spoon.
Poach the eggs directly in the soup for 3 minutes, and cover with chopped coriander to serve.

xerem-de-conquilhas.d: A porridge of cracked maize from the Algarve, crowned with cockles opened in their own juice. Cousin to polenta and American grits, it bears an Arabic-derived name, like so much in the Portuguese south.
s: Purge the cockles for two hours in salted water so they release their sand.
Fry the bacon and chorizo, add the onion, garlic and tomato, and stew for 15 minutes.
Open the cockles separately with the white wine, 3 minutes covered, then strain their liquor carefully.
Pour a litre and a half of water and the cockle liquor over the refogado, bring to the boil, then rain in the cracked maize.
Stir for 35 minutes over low heat until thick, then add the cockles and plenty of coriander off the heat.

ensopado-de-borrego.d: A lamb stew served over slices of bread that soak up the broth at the bottom of the plate. Ensopado means 'soaked': the bread is not a side dish, it is half the dish.
s: Marinate the lamb in large pieces for 4 hours in the white wine, crushed garlic, paprika and bay.
Drain, dry and sear the meat in olive oil until well coloured.
Add the sliced onion and grated tomato, let them cook down, then pour in the strained marinade.
Cover with water and simmer for 1¼ hours; add the potatoes for the last 25 minutes.
Line deep plates with slices of bread, pour the scalding stew over them and cover with fresh mint.

sericaia.d: An egg and cinnamon pudding, baked fiercely in an earthenware dish where it cracks into fissures. Served with candied Elvas plums, and its name is said to come from Serica — the ancients' name for China.
s: Infuse the milk with the lemon zest and a cinnamon stick, then strain it.
Slake the flour in a little cold milk, then pour in the hot milk while whisking and thicken for 5 minutes.
Whisk the yolks and sugar to the ribbon, fold in the warm cream, then the whites beaten to peaks.
Ladle into an earthenware dish, letting each ladleful form a wave, and dust generously with cinnamon between each.
Bake for 25 minutes at 220°C: the surface should crack deeply. Serve warm with the plums.

empadas-de-vila-vicosa.d: Small chicken pies in lard pastry, moulded in tin cups. They were sold outside mass and on the forecourts of shrines, warm, wrapped in paper.
s: Poach the hen for 1 hour with onion, garlic, bay and white wine; let it cool in its broth.
Bone it and chop the meat by knife into small pieces; mix with a little reduced broth, the nutmeg and lemon.
Knead the flour, melted lard, warm water and salt into a supple dough; rest it for 30 minutes.
Line small cylindrical moulds, fill with the mixture and cover with a disc of dough sealed with your thumb.
Glaze with egg, cut a vent and bake for 35 minutes at 190°C.

folar-de-chaves.d: A brioche loaf stuffed with four smoked meats, baked at Easter in the communal ovens. The folar was given to godchildren on Easter Sunday, in exchange for the violets offered on Palm Sunday.
s: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk, then knead with the flour, eggs, oil and salt for 15 minutes.
Prove for 1½ hours: the dough should double and stay supple, almost sticky.
Cut all the cured meats into 1 cm dice and fry them briefly so they release a little fat.
Roll out the dough, scatter over the meats and paprika, roll it up, then coil the log into a ring in a round tin.
Prove for 45 minutes, glaze with egg and bake for 45 minutes at 180°C.

cabrito-a-serrana.d: A milk-fed kid roasted in a wood oven with rice cooked in its juices, the Christmas and Easter dish of Portugal's north-east. A marinade of red wine and paprika gives it its near-black crust.
s: Marinate the kid for 12 hours in the red wine, crushed garlic, paprika, chilli and bay.
Rub the meat with lard, set it on a bed of onions in an earthenware dish and pour over the marinade.
Roast for 1½ hours at 170°C, basting every 20 minutes, then add the quartered potatoes.
Take two ladles of the juices, use them to moisten the raw rice in a separate dish with water, and bake it alongside for 25 minutes.
Raise to 220°C for ten minutes to brown the meat. Serve the kid and rice together.

pica-pau.d: Cubes of beef sautéed with white wine and mustard, served scalding with gherkins and olives, speared with forks from a dish in the middle of the table. The name means 'woodpecker': you peck at it.
s: Cut the beef into 2 cm cubes and salt them only at the last moment.
Heat the oil and butter until foaming, then sear the meat over very high heat, in small batches.
Add the crushed garlic, bay and chilli, and let them perfume the pan for 30 seconds without burning the garlic.
Deglaze with white wine, add the mustard and reduce for 3 minutes: the sauce should stay short and glossy.
Tip into a deep dish with the gherkins and olives, cover with parsley and serve with bread for mopping.

travesseiros-de-colares.d: 'Pillows' of puff pastry filled with an almond and egg cream, rolled in sugar as they leave the oven. The queue outside the Sintra pastry shop that created them has not thinned since 1943.
s: Make a puff pastry: a base of flour, iced water and salt, then three single turns with the butter, resting 30 minutes between each.
Cook the sugar and water to soft ball with the zest, then take off the heat.
Stir in the ground almonds, let it cool a little, then add the eggs and yolks off the heat.
Thicken this cream over very low heat, stirring constantly, then cool it completely.
Cut rectangles of pastry, pipe the cream along them, fold into pillows and seal. Bake for 20 minutes at 200°C and roll in sugar while still hot.

porchetta-di-ariccia.d: A whole boned pig, stuffed with herbs and roasted for five hours until the rind becomes a glazed shell. It is carved by knife in the markets of Lazio and eaten in a bread roll, with nothing else.
s: Lay the belly flat, rind down, and score the meat in a lattice without piercing the skin.
Pound the garlic, rosemary, fennel, pepper and salt into a paste, and rub it over the whole inner surface.
Lay the loin down the centre, roll tightly and tie every three centimetres.
Prick the rind all over, rub it with coarse salt and let it dry uncovered overnight in the fridge.
Roast for 4 hours at 150°C, then 45 minutes at 240°C to glaze the skin. Rest for an hour before carving.

vincisgrassi.d: The ancestor of lasagne, with poultry offal, truffle and béchamel, its recipe printed as early as 1799. The name is said to come from the Austrian prince Windisch-Graetz, then besieging Ancona.
s: Knead the flour and eggs, rest for an hour, then roll very thin sheets and blanch them for a minute.
Fry the diced ham, minced meat and offal, moisten with white wine and tomato, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the soaked and chopped porcini and give it another 20 minutes.
Make a thick béchamel with butter, flour and milk, seasoned with nutmeg.
Layer six sheets of pasta with sauce, béchamel and parmesan, grating truffle between the layers, and bake for 45 minutes at 180°C.

cacciucco.d: The fish stew of Livorno, which must contain at least five species — as many as there are C's in its name, says the harbour rule. The rockfish collapse into the sauce, the finer ones stay whole.
s: Start with the octopus and cuttlefish: they need 40 minutes, everything else needs ten.
Fry them in oil with the garlic and chilli, deglaze with red wine and let it evaporate.
Add the crushed tomato and sage, cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Pass the separately cooked rockfish through a food mill and stir that purée into the pot.
Finally add the prawns and mussels for 5 minutes. Serve over garlic-rubbed toast in a deep plate.

schlutzkrapfen.d: Rye half-moons filled with spinach and ricotta, served in browned butter with chives. The rye in the dough is what sets them apart from southern ravioli: it is the grain of the high valleys.
s: Knead the two flours, eggs, milk and salt into a firm dough; rest it for an hour under a cloth.
Wilt the spinach, squeeze it dry between your hands — not a drop should run — and chop it.
Mix it with butter-softened onion, drained ricotta and nutmeg.
Roll the dough very thin, cut 8 cm discs, fill them and fold into half-moons, pressing out the air.
Poach for 4 minutes in barely simmering water, plate and coat with browned butter, parmesan and chives.

pasta-e-fagioli.d: A poor man's dish turned emblem: beans, mismatched short pasta and olive oil. The ends of pasta packets were once tipped in, hence the mixed shapes now deliberately sought out.
s: Soak the beans overnight, then cook them for 1 hour in unsalted water with the bay and a garlic clove.
Take out a third of the beans and crush them to a purée: that is what thickens the soup without flour.
Turn the remaining garlic golden in the oil with the rosemary and chilli, then discard the rosemary.
Add the crushed tomato, the whole beans and the purée, and pour in their cooking water.
Drop in the short pasta and cook for 10 minutes, stirring: the dish should stay thick. Serve with raw oil and pecorino.

coda-alla-vaccinara.d: The oxtail of the Testaccio slaughtermen, stewed for four hours in wine and celery, lifted with cocoa and pine nuts. Paid in offal, the vaccinari built a whole cuisine out of this quinto quarto.
s: Soak the oxtail sections in cold water for an hour, then pat them dry and sear them in the oil.
Fry the chopped guanciale, onion and carrot, then return the meat and deglaze with white wine.
Add the tomato purée, the cloves and water to cover; put the lid on and simmer for 3½ hours.
Blanch the celery in lengths and add it for the last half hour.
Off the heat, stir in the pine nuts, raisins and cocoa: they give the sauce its almost sweet depth.

pane-cunzato.d: Literally 'seasoned bread': a loaf split open, doused in oil and filled with tomato, anchovy and fresh cheese. It was the meal of those who had only bread — dressed with whatever came to hand.
s: Choose a thick-crusted semolina loaf baked the same day, and split it lengthways.
Rub the crumb with a cut garlic clove and douse it generously with olive oil.
Crush the tomatoes by hand straight onto the bread, juices and all, and salt them.
Lay on the anchovies, the fresh cheese in thick slices and the stoned olives.
Scatter oregano, pepper it, close the loaf and press firmly for a minute before cutting into portions.

zuppa-gallurese.d: Despite the name it is not a soup but a gratin: stale bread soaked in mutton broth between layers of fresh cheese. It is served at Gallura weddings, where it opens the meal.
s: Make a broth by cooking the mutton for 2 hours, then strain it and keep it very hot.
Cut the bread into thick slices and let them dry: they must soak without collapsing.
Grate the pecorino and slice the fresh cheese.
Layer bread, cheeses, herbs and a ladle of broth in a buttered dish, three storeys high.
The bread should be soaked but not swimming. Bake for 40 minutes at 180°C: a golden crust forms, the base stays melting.

fideua.d: A paella in which vermicelli replaces the rice. The story goes that a ship's cook, out of rice and tired of the captain serving himself first, tried pasta to put him off — the captain loved it.
s: Fry the diced cuttlefish in the paella pan, then the prawns for one minute only; set them aside.
Add the garlic, the soaked ñora pulp and the grated tomato, and reduce to a sofrito.
Tip in the broken vermicelli and toast them dry for two minutes: this stops them sticking.
Moisten with boiling saffron stock — twice the volume of pasta — and cook for 8 minutes over high heat.
Arrange the seafood on top and bake for 6 minutes at 220°C: the vermicelli ends should stand upright. Serve with aioli.

lacon-con-grelos.d: Salted pork shoulder cooked with bitter turnip tops, chorizo and potatoes. The dish of the Galician carnival: it is served only between Saint Anthony's day and Ash Wednesday.
s: Soak the salted shoulder for 36 hours in cold water, changing it five or six times.
Simmer it for 2 hours with the bay, in water that is never salted.
Blanch the turnip tops for 5 minutes in separate water and throw that water away: this removes the excess bitterness without making them bland.
Add them to the broth with the whole chorizos for 30 minutes, then the potatoes for 25 minutes.
Serve on a wooden board: the meat cut thick, the greens drained, the chorizo in rounds and the potatoes, dressed with paprika oil.

gazpachos-manchegos.d: Nothing to do with the cold soup: this is a game stew served on an unleavened flatbread broken into pieces. La Mancha shepherds cooked it on the flatbread itself, which served as the plate.
s: Joint the rabbit and chicken into small pieces and colour them in the oil with the garlic.
Add the onion, grated tomato, mushrooms and the paprika, the latter off the heat.
Pour in two litres of water, add rosemary, thyme and bay, and cook for 45 minutes.
Break the flatbread by hand into uneven 4 cm pieces and drop them into the broth.
Cook for 20 minutes, stirring: the bread absorbs almost all the liquid. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

zarangollo.d: Courgettes and onions cooked down slowly then bound with egg, barely scrambled. The market gardens of the Murcian huerta in a pan: three ingredients, and the skill is in not rushing them.
s: Slice the onions and soften them covered in the oil for 20 minutes, without letting them colour.
Cut the courgettes into thin rounds, unpeeled, and add them with a pinch of salt.
Cover and let them give up their water for 15 minutes, then uncover and let it evaporate entirely.
Crack the eggs straight into the pan and barely stir: they should stay in visible ribbons, not become an omelette.
Cut the heat as soon as the egg sets and serve warm, on toast.

pote-gallego.d: The Galician one-pot with grelos — the bitter turnip tops that grow in winter — with beans, potatoes and pork. It is the meal that waited for pilgrims at the end of the road.
s: Desalt the ribs, bacon and ear for 12 hours in cold water; soak the beans the same night.
Put the meats and beans in cold water, bring to a simmer and skim carefully.
Cook for 1½ hours at a gentle boil, then lift out the meats and keep them warm.
Add the washed and roughly chopped greens, then the potatoes broken by hand, and cook for 30 minutes.
Return the cut-up meats, add the sliced chorizo for 15 minutes and serve everything from the pot.

torrijas.d: Stale bread soaked in sweetened milk, coated in egg and fried, then rolled in cinnamon. A Holy Week recipe, mentioned as early as the 15th century as a restorative for women who had just given birth.
s: Infuse the milk with 100 g of sugar, the zest and a cinnamon stick, then let it cool a little.
Cut the bread into 3 cm slices, ideally the day before: too fresh and it falls apart.
Soak each slice for 30 seconds a side — no longer — and let them drain on a rack for 10 minutes.
Coat them in beaten egg and fry in hot oil, 2 minutes a side, until well coloured.
Roll them at once in cinnamon sugar, or pour over honey loosened with red wine.

himmelstorte.d: Two sponge discs capped with crisp meringue, separated by cream and sharp redcurrants. The contrast between the sugar of the meringue and the acidity of the fruit is the whole point of the cake.
s: Cream the butter with 100 g of sugar, add the yolks, milk, flour and baking powder.
Spread this batter thinly in two 24 cm tins.
Beat the whites to very firm peaks with 200 g of sugar, spread them over the raw batter and scatter flaked almonds.
Bake for 30 minutes at 160°C: the meringue should dry without browning. Cool in the tins.
Whip the cream with the vanilla, spread it and the redcurrants over the first disc, and top with the second, meringue upwards.

birnen-bohnen-speck.d: Green beans, whole cooking pears and smoked bacon in a single pan. The pairing seems improbable in southern Germany and self-evident in the north, where it marks the end of summer.
s: Cook the smoked bacon for 20 minutes in a litre of water, at a bare simmer.
Set the whole unpeeled pears on the bacon and poach them for 15 minutes: they should stay firm.
Add the trimmed beans and the savory, and continue for 15 minutes.
Boil the potatoes separately in salted water.
Thicken the broth with a spoonful of slaked flour, sharpen with a dash of vinegar and a pinch of sugar, and serve everything together.

zwiebelkuchen.d: A thick tart of onions in cream with caraway, eaten in September with Federweisser, the new wine still fermenting in the glass. The two are found only together, and only for a month a year.
s: Knead the flour, the yeast dissolved in warm water, the butter and salt, and prove for an hour.
Slice the onions and soften them covered for 30 minutes in the butter, without colouring: they should turn translucent.
Add the diced bacon and let everything cool completely.
Mix the sour cream, eggs, a spoonful of flour and the caraway, then fold in the onions.
Line a deep tin with the dough, fill to 3 cm and bake for 45 minutes at 190°C.

salzburger-nockerl.d: Three domes of sweet soufflé said to represent the hills around Salzburg. They must be served within two minutes: after that the mountains sink and the effect is lost.
s: Butter an oval dish, pour in the milk and jam, and heat on the hob until simmering.
Whip the six whites to very firm peaks, adding the sugar in three stages.
Fold in three yolks, the sifted flour, vanilla and zest, lifting rather than stirring.
Spoon three large mounds of the mixture into the hot dish, forming three distinct domes.
Bake for 10 minutes at 200°C: the peaks should brown and the inside stay runny. Dust and serve at once.

buendnerfleisch.d: Beef cured with mountain herbs then air-dried for months in the dry Alpine air, pressed regularly to give it its square shape. It is sliced so thinly it turns translucent.
s: Trim the beef of all fat and sinew: only pure muscle dries properly.
Pound the salt, juniper, bay, thyme, rosemary, pepper and garlic, and rub the meat all over.
Put it in a covered container and cure it for three weeks in the cold, turning it every two days.
Rinse, pat dry, wrap in a cloth and hang it in a cool, dry, airy place for five to eight weeks.
Press it flat under a weight once a week. Slice it at the last moment, paper-thin, and serve on buttered rye bread.

papet-vaudois.d: A stew of leeks and potatoes topped with a cabbage sausage cooked in it. The leek must literally vanish: papet comes from papette, porridge.
s: Slice the whole leeks, white and green, and soften them in the butter with the onion for 20 minutes, covered.
Deglaze with white wine, let it evaporate, then add the potatoes in large cubes and the broth.
Simmer for 40 minutes over low heat: the leeks should collapse and the potatoes barely crush.
Lay the cabbage sausages on top, without pricking them, cover and poach for 30 minutes.
Lift out the sausages, enrich the papet with the cream and serve them on top, whole.

stifado.d: A beef stew with whole small onions, cinnamon and vinegar, in which the onions weigh as much as the meat. The word comes from the Venetian stufado: Venice long held the Greek coasts.
s: Scald the small onions for a minute: the skin will then come away without damaging them.
Sear the meat in large cubes in the oil, in small batches, then set aside.
Brown the whole onions in the same oil, without stirring, until golden on all sides.
Return the meat, deglaze with the wine and vinegar, and add the tomato, spices and sugar.
Cover and simmer for 2¼ hours without ever stirring with a spoon — shake the pot instead, or the onions would break up.

saganaki-crevettes.d: Prawns cooked in tomato with feta, in the small two-handled pan that gives the dish its name. The feta does not really melt: it softens and salts the sauce at the same time.
s: Peel the prawns, keeping the tails, and make a quick stock with the heads and shells.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil, add the crushed tomato and chilli, and reduce for 15 minutes.
Moisten with a ladle of the strained stock and let it thicken.
Add the prawns, flame with ouzo and cook them for barely 3 minutes: any longer and they turn rubbery.
Crumble the feta coarsely over, grill for 5 minutes and serve scalding, with bread for mopping.

afelia.d: Pork stewed in red wine with crushed coriander seed — a great deal of it, the Cypriot signature. Served with bulgur pilaf and sheep's yogurt.
s: Crush the coriander seeds coarsely in a mortar: ground, they would lose all their scent.
Marinate the diced pork for 12 hours in the red wine with two thirds of the coriander.
Drain, pat dry and colour the meat in the oil over high heat.
Pour in the marinade, add the cinnamon and remaining coriander, cover and simmer for 1 hour.
For the pilaf, brown the broken vermicelli in oil, add the bulgur and broth, and let it swell for 15 minutes, covered.

lampuki-pie.d: A pie of dorado, the fish Malta catches from August to December beneath rafts of floating palm fronds. The fish shares the crust with spinach, olives and cauliflower: a late-summer pie, never served out of season.
s: Flour the fish slices and fry them for two minutes a side, then bone them and flake the flesh.
Soften the onion and garlic, add the tomato and reduce for 15 minutes.
Blanch the cauliflower in small florets and wilt the spinach; squeeze both thoroughly dry.
Combine all the vegetables with the sauce, olives, capers and mint, then fold in the fish without breaking it up.
Line a tin, fill it, cover with a pastry lid, glaze with egg and bake for 45 minutes at 190°C.

sarma-bosniaque.d: Sour cabbage leaves rolled around meat and rice, stewed for two hours on a bed of smoked ribs. The cabbage is fermented whole, in heads, in barrels — every Bosnian family keeps one in the cellar.
s: Separate the leaves of the fermented cabbage, rinse them if very sour and flatten the central rib with a knife.
Soften the onion, let it cool, then mix with the meats, raw rice, garlic, egg and paprika.
Place a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll tightly, tucking in the ends.
Line a pot with the smoked ribs and chopped cabbage, and pack the rolls upright, tightly.
Cover with water, set a plate on top to hold them down, and simmer for 2 hours. Thicken with a lard and paprika roux at the end.

jota-triestina.d: A soup of beans, sauerkraut and potato, on the border of three cuisines: Italian, Slovene and Austrian. Trieste was the Habsburg port, and its cooking never picked a side.
s: Soak the beans overnight, then cook them for 1 hour with the smoked ribs and bay.
Cook the sauerkraut separately in a little water with the cumin for 40 minutes: cooked with the beans, its acidity would toughen them.
Add the potatoes in large cubes to the beans and continue for 25 minutes.
Crush a third of the beans and potatoes with a fork to thicken the soup.
Make a brown roux of lard, flour, onion and garlic, stir it into the pot with the sauerkraut, and let it marry for 20 minutes.

gibanica.d: Sheets of pastry crumpled and layered with fresh cheese and eggs, baked until golden and puffed. The name comes from gibati, to fold: the pastry is never smooth, always crumpled.
s: Mash the cheeses with a fork and mix with the beaten eggs and half the sour cream.
Butter a dish and lay two sheets of pastry flat, letting them overhang.
Dip the next sheets briefly in the mixture, crumple them by hand and arrange them in waves in the dish.
Alternate until everything is used, finishing with two smooth sheets folded over the top.
Mix the remaining cream with the sparkling water, pour it over the pie and bake for 50 minutes at 180°C. Let it cool a little before cutting.

jagnjetina-ispod-sacha.d: Lamb and potatoes cooked under a cast-iron bell buried in embers. The sač is found across the Balkans, but Montenegro has made it the obligatory meal of family reunions.
s: Stud the lamb with slivers of garlic and rub it with oil, rosemary and salt an hour ahead.
Cut the potatoes and vegetables into large pieces: small ones would dissolve over two and a half hours.
Arrange everything in a wide cast-iron dish and pour over the white wine and a glass of water.
Cover with the bell and bury it under embers, or bake at 200°C under a heavy lid.
Cook for 2 hours without ever lifting it, then uncover for 20 minutes to brown. Serve with kajmak.

jota-slovene.d: A soup of pearl barley and beans with smoked pork, thick enough to hold a spoon. It was the soup of Austro-Hungarian soldiers, served in every barracks of the Empire, and Slovenia kept it for itself.
s: Soak the barley and beans separately overnight.
Put them in cold water with the smoked ribs and bay, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the carrot, celeriac and potato in dice, and continue for 30 minutes.
Make a pale roux with the lard, flour, onion and garlic, and stir it into the pot.
Shred the meat, return it, add the marjoram and let it marry for 10 minutes. The soup should be very thick.

pierogi-ruskie-zapiekane.d: Polish dumplings filled with buckwheat, lentils and mushrooms — the Lenten version, without meat or cheese. Buckwheat, kasza gryczana, is to eastern Poland what the potato is to the west.
s: Knead the flour, warm water, egg and salt for 10 minutes, then rest for 40 minutes under a cloth.
Cook the buckwheat and lentils separately, and soak the mushrooms for an hour.
Turn two onions golden in the butter, add the chopped mushrooms, then mix with the buckwheat, lentils and marjoram.
Roll the dough to 2 mm, cut 8 cm discs, fill them and seal by pinching firmly.
Poach for 4 minutes, then fry them golden with the third onion, sliced. Serve with the sour cream.

koprovka.d: Boiled beef under a white dill sauce, sweet-sour with vinegar and sugar, with a hard-boiled egg and knedlíky. The Czech canteen dish par excellence, loved and mocked in equal measure.
s: Cook the brisket for 1¾ hours with the vegetables, bay and allspice; keep the strained broth.
Make a pale roux with the butter and flour, without letting it colour, and whisk in a litre of hot broth.
Cook for 15 minutes over low heat to lose the floury taste, then add the cream.
Chop the dill very finely and add it off the heat: cooked, it loses all its scent.
Balance with vinegar and sugar — the sauce should be frankly sweet-sour — and serve over the sliced meat with half a hard-boiled egg and knedlíky.

szegedi-gulyas.d: Pork with paprika and sauerkraut, enriched with sour cream. It owes nothing to the town of Szeged but to József Székely, a Hungarian archivist who, arriving late at the inn, was served a mixture of leftovers.
s: Soften the finely sliced onions in the lard for 20 minutes, until they collapse.
Take off the heat, stir in the paprika at once: scorched, it would make the dish bitter.
Add the diced pork, garlic, caraway and tomato, moisten with a glass of water and simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add the rinsed and squeezed sauerkraut, and continue for 40 minutes.
Slacken the sour cream with the flour and a ladle of warm juices, stir in off the heat and never let it boil again.

bryndzove-pirohy.d: Potato dumplings filled with bryndza, the salty fresh sheep's cheese of the Tatra shepherds' huts. Doused in melted bacon fat and sour cream, with no pretence at lightness.
s: Boil the potatoes, rice them and let them cool completely.
Knead with the flour, eggs and salt, without working them long: overworked, the dough turns elastic.
Mash the bryndza with a fork, a little sour cream and the grated onion.
Roll the dough to 3 mm, cut 7 cm discs, fill them and seal carefully, pushing out the air.
Poach for 5 minutes in simmering water, drain and pour over crisped lardons with their fat, cream and chives.

smorrebrod-roget-al.d: The grandest of Danish open sandwiches: smoked eel, firm scrambled egg and chives on black rye bread. The order of the layers is codified, and one never eats two smørrebrød out of sequence.
s: Choose a dense rye loaf, barely sliced: it must hold the topping without bending.
Beat the eggs with the cream and a pinch of salt, then set them over a bain-marie, stirring constantly.
The eggs should stay creamy but hold on a spoon: too loose and they would soak the bread.
Butter the bread generously right to the edges — the butter is a barrier against moisture.
Lay on the eggs, then the smoked eel fillets, the chives, a few radish slices and a squeeze of lemon.

palt.d: Large dumplings of raw potato stuffed with pork, poached for an hour and served with butter and lingonberry jam. The dish of the Swedish north, dense and sustaining, that sees you through a whole day.
s: Grate the raw potatoes very finely and squeeze them in a cloth: keep the starch that settles at the bottom of the liquid.
Mix the squeezed pulp, the recovered starch, both flours and the salt into a sticky dough.
Dice the bacon, fry it with the onion and allspice, then let it cool.
Shape fist-sized balls around a spoonful of the pork, sealing them well.
Poach for 1 hour in barely simmering salted water; they float long before they are cooked. Serve with butter and lingonberry.

kalarullad.d: Blanched cabbage leaves rolled around a filling of pork and barley, browned in the oven and doused in sour cream. Barley stands in for rice: it grew where rice never reached.
s: Cut out the cabbage core and plunge the whole head into boiling water for 8 minutes; peel off the leaves as they soften.
Cook the pearl barley for 25 minutes and let it cool.
Mix the minced pork, barley, softened onion, egg, marjoram, salt and pepper.
Flatten the rib of each leaf, fill and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Pack the rolls in a buttered dish, cover with lardons and broth, and bake for 50 minutes at 180°C. Coat with sour cream thickened with flour.

sildi-kartuli.d: A cold layered dish of salt herring, potato, egg and beetroot, bound with mayonnaise and served in bright pink strata. The obligatory Baltic New Year dish, assembled the day before so it sets.
s: Boil the potatoes, carrots and beetroot separately in their skins, then cool them completely.
Dice the herring fillets small and marinate the chopped onion for 15 minutes in the vinegar and sugar.
Grate each vegetable coarsely into a separate bowl: the colours must never mix.
Build up in a dish: herring, onion, potato, mayonnaise, carrot, egg, mayonnaise, beetroot.
Smooth the top, cover and chill for 12 hours. Decorate with dill and grated egg to serve.

kotleti-pozharskie.d: Poultry croquettes coated in cubes of bread rather than crumbs, which makes them bristle as they fry. Pushkin recommended them in a letter in verse: 'dine at leisure at Pozharsky's in Torzhok'.
s: Chop the poultry by knife into small dice: a mincer would turn it into an elastic paste.
Mix it with cold butter in flakes, the cream, softened and cooled onion, nutmeg and salt; chill for an hour to firm up.
Cut stale bread into tiny 3 mm cubes, crusts removed: this is the true coating.
Shape slightly domed cutlets, flour them, dip in beaten egg then roll in the bread cubes.
Fry them 4 minutes a side in clarified butter over medium heat, then finish 6 minutes in a 180°C oven.

rasstegai.d: Small pies left open at the top, into which a spoonful of scalding broth is poured just before serving. The name comes from rasstegnut, 'to unfasten': the pie stays ajar like an unbuttoned collar.
s: Dissolve the yeast in warm milk with the sugar, let it froth, then knead with the flour, butter, one egg and salt. Prove for 1½ hours.
Cook the rice in salted water and let it cool completely.
Dice the fish, mix with the rice, butter-softened onion and dill; season with plenty of pepper.
Divide the dough into 60 g balls, flatten, fill and pinch the edges shut, leaving an oval opening at the centre.
Glaze with egg and bake for 22 minutes at 200°C. Pour a spoonful of scalding fish stock into each opening as you serve.

deruny.d: The Ukrainian potato pancakes, fried golden in lard and served under a spoonful of sour cream. The town of Korosten holds an annual festival in their honour, complete with a monument.
s: Grate the potatoes finely and the onion with them: its acidity stops them darkening.
Let them drain for ten minutes in a colander, without pressing, then recover the starch settled at the bottom of the bowl.
Mix pulp, starch, eggs, flour, salt and pepper: the batter should be thick and barely pourable.
Heat the lard and drop in flattened spoonfuls; let them set for 4 minutes untouched.
Turn, brown for 3 minutes, and serve scalding with sour cream, garlic-fried mushrooms and dill.

draniki-kolduny.d: Grated potato cakes enclosing a meat filling — the stuffed version of draniki. The word kolduny means 'sorcerers': you never know what they conceal until you bite.
s: Fry the minced pork with one onion and the marjoram, salt generously and let it cool.
Grate the potatoes and the second onion, drain them and recover the starch from the bottom.
Mix with the egg, flour and salt: the batter should hold on a spatula.
Drop a spoonful of batter into the hot lard, hollow it, add a nut of filling and cover with a little more batter.
Brown for 5 minutes a side over medium heat — any hotter and the outside would burn before the centre cooked. Serve with sour cream and lardons.

scouse.d: A stew of lamb and potato brought by Norwegian sailors as lapskaus. The people of Liverpool took their nickname from it — Scousers — and their accent bears the same name.
s: Brown both meats in large pieces in a heavy pot, in small batches.
Add the onions and carrots in thick rounds, then the broth, bay, thyme and Worcestershire.
Simmer covered for 1½ hours, untouched.
Add half the potatoes in large pieces and the other half grated: the grated ones collapse and thicken the stew.
Continue for 45 minutes. Serve with pickled red cabbage, beetroot and bread — that is the tradition, and it is not up for discussion.

bara-brith.d: The Welsh 'speckled bread', its dried fruit steeped overnight in black tea. The tea replaces the fat: this loaf contains not an ounce of butter, and is buttered on the plate instead.
s: Steep the raisins and chopped prunes in the hot tea with the brown sugar, overnight.
By morning the fruit should have drunk nearly all the liquid and trebled in size.
Work in the beaten eggs, zest and spices, then the flour and baking powder, without overworking.
Pour into a lined loaf tin and bake for 1¼ hours at 160°C; cover with paper if the top colours too fast.
Brush with warm honey as it comes out and let it cool for a full day before slicing. Eaten buttered.

dublin-coddle.d: Sausages and bacon poached — never grilled — with potatoes and onions in a pale broth. It was the Thursday night dish, made with leftovers before Friday's abstinence from meat.
s: Poach the sausages and bacon for 5 minutes in boiling water, then throw that water away: this is what gives coddle its characteristic pallor.
Layer in a pot: onions, potatoes in large pieces, carrots, sausages and bacon.
Moisten with the broth and stout to cover only three quarters of the way up.
Add the bay, cover and simmer for 1¾ hours over very low heat, without ever stirring.
The potatoes on top stay whole, those at the bottom collapse and thicken the broth. Cover with parsley.

asperges-a-la-flamande.d: White asparagus under melted butter with crushed hard-boiled egg, which each diner mixes on their own plate. Mechelen is Belgium's white asparagus capital, grown under ridges to stay pale.
s: Peel the asparagus from tip to base, twice over, and snap off the fibrous end.
Simmer the peelings for 15 minutes in salted water: this fragrant broth will poach the spears.
Poach them for 15 minutes depending on thickness, then drain on a cloth — never in a colander, they would break.
Melt the butter until it just begins to turn nutty, then take it off the heat.
Crush the hard-boiled eggs into the warm butter with the parsley, nutmeg and lemon. Each diner mixes it on their own plate.

rommegrot.d: A porridge of sour cream worked until the butter separates and rises in golden pools. Served with that butter, sugar and cinnamon; it marked harvest feasts and births.
s: Bring the sour cream to a simmer in a heavy pan and let it bubble gently, covered, for 10 minutes.
Rain in half the flour while whisking, and keep stirring: after a few minutes the butter starts to bead on the surface.
Spoon off that butter and keep it: it is what will be poured over the porridge at the end.
Add the rest of the flour, then the hot milk little by little, whisking to a smooth glossy cream.
Cook for 15 minutes over low heat, salt it, and serve with the reserved butter, sugar and cinnamon.

kalakeitto-saaristo.d: A soup of Baltic white fish with milk and allspice, without cream. The Finnish archipelago islands make it the plain, clear version of lohikeitto, with whatever the nets bring in.
s: Fillet the fish and make a stock with the heads and bones for 20 minutes with the bay and allspice; strain it.
Sweat the onion and carrot in butter without colouring, then add the diced potatoes.
Moisten with the stock and cook for 15 minutes.
Pour in the milk and bring to a bare simmer — boiling would curdle it — then slide in the fish pieces.
Cut the heat and let them poach for 8 minutes in the residual warmth. Add a large handful of dill and serve with buttered rye bread.

ciorba-radauteana.d: A chicken soup whitened with cream and egg yolk, invented in 1979 by a cook in Rădăuți who wanted a gentle version of tripe soup. It conquered the country within a decade.
s: Poach the chicken for 40 minutes with the whole vegetables and bay, skimming: the broth must stay clear.
Lift out the meat and cut it into fine strips; julienne the carrot and discard the other vegetables.
Pound the garlic with salt and two spoonfuls of broth.
Beat the cream and yolks, temper them with a ladle of hot broth trickled in, then thicken the soup off the heat.
Sharpen it with vinegar, add the garlic and parsley, and never let it boil again.

selsko-meso.d: Pork, mushrooms and sheep's white cheese baked in an individual earthenware pan, the tavče. 'Village meat': each guest gets their own dish, brought from the oven still bubbling.
s: Cut the pork into fine strips and sear it briskly in oil, in small batches, so it colours rather than stews.
Add the onion in half-moons and the pepper, then the sliced mushrooms, and let them release their water.
Deglaze with white wine, add the crushed tomato, savory and paprika off the heat.
Divide between earthenware pans, crumble the cheese over and break half an egg onto each.
Bake for 25 minutes at 220°C: the top should gratinate and the rim of the pan crackle. Serve in the dish it cooked in.

kapama-bansko.d: Four meats, rice and sauerkraut packed into a jar sealed with dough and baked for three hours in the village oven. Kapama comes from the Turkish kapamak, 'to cover': nothing must escape.
s: Brown the chicken, pork and veal separately in the lard, then the sliced sausage.
Fry the onions, add the paprika off the heat and the savory.
Squeeze the sauerkraut and line the base of an earthenware jar with it; alternate meats, raw rice and sauerkraut to the top.
Moisten with a litre of sauerkraut juice let down with water, without going above the level of the ingredients.
Knead a dough of flour and water, seal the lid hermetically with it and bake for 3 hours at 160°C. The seal is broken at the table.

shuizhu-yu.d: The name promises boiling water and delivers a lake of red oil: slivers of fish poached under an avalanche of dried chilli and Sichuan pepper. The oil layer is not a sauce, it is a thermal lid.
s: Fillet the fish and slice it thinly on the bias; massage with the egg white, starch and rice wine, and leave for 20 minutes.
Blanch the bean sprouts for a minute and lay them in the bottom of a large bowl.
Fry the doubanjiang in a little oil until it turns red, add the garlic and ginger, then the broth.
Poach the fish slices one by one for barely 90 seconds: they whiten and rise. Pour everything over the sprouts.
Heat the remaining oil with the dried chillies and Sichuan pepper until smoking, and pour it scalding over the fish.

char-siu.d: Cantonese lacquered pork, red and glossy, hanging on hooks in shop windows. Char siu means 'fork roasted': the meat was threaded on long skewers and cooked over the fire, never laid down.
s: Cut the pork into long strips 5 cm thick: that shape allows caramelisation on every side.
Mix all the marinade ingredients except half the honey, and marinate the meat for 24 hours.
Roast on a rack over a tray of water for 30 minutes at 200°C.
Turn, brush with marinade and continue for 20 minutes.
Brush with the remaining honey and grill for 8 minutes, watching closely: the lacquer should brown in patches without burning.

dongpo-rou.d: Cubes of pork belly braised for three hours in Shaoxing wine until the fat turns translucent. Su Dongpo, an 11th-century poet and governor, is said to have given it to the labourers dredging West Lake.
s: Blanch the whole belly for 5 minutes, rinse it and cut it into 5 cm cubes with the rind.
Line the base of a pot with spring onion stalks and ginger slices: the meat must never touch the metal.
Pack the cubes rind upwards, tightly, in a single layer.
Pour in the rice wine, soy sauce and sugar, add the star anise and cinnamon, and cover.
Simmer for 2½ hours over very low heat, then steam each cube for 20 minutes. The rind should wobble.

jianbing.d: A grain crêpe spread with a wooden rake on a scorching griddle, cracked with an egg, folded around a crisp cracker. The Chinese street breakfast par excellence, served in ninety seconds.
s: Whisk the three flours into the water to a very thin batter, and rest for 30 minutes.
Fry the wonton squares until they puff and crisp; drain them.
Pour a ladle of batter onto an oiled griddle and spread it into a very thin circle with a circular sweep.
Crack an egg on top, spread it with a spatula, scatter sesame, spring onion and coriander, then flip the crêpe.
Brush with hoisin and chilli oil, lay the crisp cracker in the centre, fold into quarters and serve at once.

guilin-mifen.d: Rice noodles in a broth of fermented bamboo shoots, whose powerful smell reaches you several metres before the bowl. Locals find it irresistible; visitors sometimes need a mouthful to come round.
s: Blanch the pork bones, rinse them, then simmer for 3 hours with the ginger, star anise and dried fish.
Strain the broth: it should be cloudy and deeply fragrant.
Fry the fermented bamboo shoots for two minutes in oil — this is the moment their smell is released — then tip them into the broth.
Fry the peanuts in oil until golden, and drain them.
Cook the rice noodles for 3 minutes, put them in bowls, pour over the scalding broth and top with bamboo, pickled beans, peanuts, sprouts and herbs.

foshan-fotiaoqiang.d: A soup of eighteen ingredients simmered in a jar sealed with Shaoxing wine. The name comes from a poem: a monk, catching the scent over the monastery wall, is said to have vaulted the fence to taste it.
s: Soak the shiitake, dried scallops and dried shrimp separately overnight; keep all the soaking liquids.
Blanch each meat separately, rinse it, then fry it briefly with ginger.
Layer the ingredients in a jar, longest-cooking at the bottom, most delicate on top: meats below, seafood above.
Pour in the rice wine, broth and strained soaking liquids, filling no more than three quarters.
Seal the jar with oiled paper and string, and steam gently for 5 hours. Open it at the table: the scent is half the dish.

guoqiao-mixian.d: A broth so rich that a film of oil keeps it scalding, into which raw meats and vegetables are dipped at the table. A wife carried her husband's meal this way to an island where he studied — the bridge was long, the soup stayed hot.
s: Simmer the chicken and pork bones for 2 hours with ginger and spring onion, then strain: the broth must keep a layer of fat on top.
Slice the raw meats almost transparently thin, under 2 mm: that is what allows them to cook on contact.
Arrange the raw meats, mushrooms, sprouts and chives on separate plates.
Cook the rice noodles and keep them warm in a separate bowl.
Bring the broth to 95°C, pour it into a large scalding bowl, and add the ingredients at the table: meats first, noodles last.

suan-cai-yu.d: Freshwater fish stewed with fermented Chinese cabbage in large earthenware pots. China's north-east ferments cabbage by the barrel before winter, like Poland or Alsace, and for the same reason.
s: Rinse the fermented cabbage, squeeze it and cut it into very fine shreds: the finer it is, the more sourness it gives the broth.
Fry the pork belly in lardons until it renders its fat, then add ginger, garlic and spring onion.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry for 10 minutes over high heat: this dry stage is what concentrates the flavour.
Pour in the rice wine, soy sauce and broth, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Slide in the fish sections, the tofu and the glass noodles, and poach for 10 minutes without stirring. Season with white pepper.

thukpa-tibetain.d: A soup of hand-pulled noodles in yak broth, thickened with roasted barley flour. At four thousand metres water boils at 87°C: everything cooks slowly, and nothing is eaten cold.
s: Knead the flour, water and salt for 15 minutes, oil the dough and rest it for an hour under a bowl.
Simmer the diced beef for 45 minutes with ginger, garlic and Sichuan pepper.
Add the onion, carrot and daikon in large pieces, and continue for 20 minutes.
Pull the dough by hand into long ribbons, stretching and folding it several times, then drop them straight into the broth.
Cook for 5 minutes, thicken with a spoonful of slaked barley flour, and cover with coriander and spring onion.

wenchang-ji.d: A chicken barely poached, then plunged into iced water so the skin turns gelatinous, and served cold with ginger sauce. It is the direct ancestor of Singapore's Hainanese chicken rice.
s: Rub the chicken with coarse salt inside and out, and leave it for an hour at room temperature.
Lower it into a large pan of simmering water with ginger and spring onion, cut the heat and poach covered for 40 minutes, never boiling.
Lift it out and plunge it straight into an iced water bath for ten minutes: the skin contracts and turns firm and translucent.
Cook the rice in the poaching broth with the garlic and a little chicken fat.
Chop the ginger and spring onion very finely, salt them, and pour smoking oil over. Carve the cold chicken and serve with the sauce and rice.

okonomiyaki.d: In Hiroshima the pancake is not mixed but built in layers: crêpe, mountain of cabbage, noodles, egg. The Osaka version mixes everything; the two cities have argued about it for seventy years.
s: Whisk the flour and water into a thin batter and rest it for 30 minutes.
Pour a ladle onto the griddle and spread it into a thin circle; pile finely shredded cabbage and sprouts on top.
Lay on the bacon slices, drizzle a little batter to bind, and flip the whole thing in one movement — this is the difficult part.
Cook covered for 8 minutes: the cabbage halves in volume as it steams.
Alongside, fry the noodles with a little sauce, cook an egg into a thin omelette, stack noodles, pancake and egg, then coat with sauce and mayonnaise.

oden.d: A Japanese one-pot in which each ingredient simmers for hours in a clear dashi and soy broth. It is sold in convenience stores in winter, and everyone picks with tongs from the steaming tray.
s: Peel the daikon into thick rounds, bevel the edges with a knife and pre-cook it for 30 minutes in rice water: it loses its bitterness.
Make the broth with dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar; it should stay clear and barely salty.
Hard-boil the eggs, blanch the konjac and briefly grill the tofu.
Add the ingredients by cooking time: daikon and octopus first, for two hours; eggs and tofu next; fish cakes last.
Never let it boil: the broth should barely tremble. Serve with a dab of yellow mustard.

unadon.d: Grilled lacquered eel over a bowl of rice, eaten on the midsummer Day of the Ox to withstand the heat. The sauce in old houses is never thrown away: it has been topped up for generations.
s: Reduce the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar by half: this is the tare, the base sauce.
Butterfly the eel, remove the backbone and cut it into bowl-sized sections.
Steam it first for 10 minutes, flesh side up: this is what makes it melting and renders the fat.
Then grill it over embers, dipping it three times in the tare between passes, until the lacquer shines.
Serve over hot vinegared rice, spoon over a little sauce and dust with sanshō pepper.

kaiseki-chawanmushi.d: A savoury dashi custard steamed in a lidded cup, so tender it must be eaten with a spoon. It is the only Japanese dish eaten hot with a spoon, and that alone makes it singular.
s: Beat the eggs without frothing them: the smallest bubble would give a grainy texture.
Mix them with the cooled dashi, soy sauce and mirin, in a ratio of one part egg to three parts broth.
Pass the mixture through a fine sieve, twice: that is what gives the velvet texture.
Divide chicken, prawns, shiitake and ginkgo nuts between the cups, pour in the mixture and cover.
Steam for 12 minutes over gentle heat with the lid ajar: above 85°C the custard turns holey.

motsunabe.d: A pot of beef tripe, cabbage and garlic chives in a broth of garlic and chilli. Born in post-war Fukuoka, when offal was all there was, it became the city's winter dish.
s: Blanch the tripe for 10 minutes, rinse it in cold water and cut it into 4 cm pieces.
Cook it for 40 minutes in the dashi with half the garlic and the ginger, until tender.
Season the broth with soy sauce and miso, without boiling it once the miso is in.
Arrange the cabbage in large pieces, the tofu and the tripe in the pot, and crown with a mountain of garlic chives and sliced garlic.
Bring to a simmer at the table for 10 minutes. Finish the broth with ramen noodles — the shime, the closing of the meal.

zunda-mochi.d: Glutinous rice cakes under a sweetened purée of edamame, brilliant green. The name may come from zuda, the pestle: Tōhoku farmers pounded fresh beans in a mortar after the summer harvest.
s: Soak the glutinous rice overnight, then steam it for 40 minutes over a cloth.
Pod the edamame, blanch them for 4 minutes and slip the second skin off each bean — tedious, and what gives the colour.
Pound the beans in a mortar with the sugar and a pinch of salt, adding a little water: the purée should stay slightly grainy.
Pound the hot rice in a mortar until it becomes an elastic mass with no visible grain.
Shape balls with hands wetted in starch and coat them in the green purée. Eat the same day.

samgyetang.d: A whole young chicken stuffed with glutinous rice, ginseng and jujubes, poached until it collapses. It is eaten on the hottest days of summer — Korean logic holds that heat is fought with heat.
s: Soak the glutinous rice for 2 hours, then drain it.
Clean the inside of the chicken thoroughly and stuff it with rice, ginseng, jujubes, garlic and chestnuts, filling only two thirds.
Close the opening by crossing the legs, or sew it: the rice swells and would otherwise escape.
Cover with cold water, bring to a simmer and skim, then poach for 1¼ hours without ever boiling.
Serve the whole chicken in its broth, unsalted: each diner seasons from a saucer of salt and pepper, to taste.

jjajangmyeon.d: Noodles under a black sauce of fried soybean paste, pork and onion. Born in Incheon's Chinatown around 1905, it became so Korean that on 14 April single people eat it dressed in black.
s: Fry the black bean paste in oil for 4 minutes over low heat: this step removes its bitterness, and cannot be skipped.
Fry the diced pork with the ginger, then add the onion, courgette and potato in small cubes.
Sweat for 10 minutes: the onion must give up its sugar, and the sauce depends on it.
Add the fried paste and a glass of water, simmer for 10 minutes, then thicken with slaked starch.
Cook the noodles, plate them, pour the sauce over and crown with finely julienned cucumber.

galbijjim.d: Beef short ribs braised in a sweet soy sauce with radish, carrot, jujubes and chestnuts. A dish for great Korean occasions, served at Chuseok and weddings, never on an ordinary day.
s: Soak the ribs for 2 hours in cold water, changing it twice: this is what gives a clear sauce.
Blanch them for 10 minutes, discard the water and rinse each piece carefully.
Blend the pear, onion, garlic and ginger: the pear's enzymes tenderise the meat better than any amount of cooking.
Mix this purée with the soy sauce and sugar, pour it over the meat and marinate for 4 hours.
Braise covered for 1½ hours, then add the radish, turned carrots, jujubes, chestnuts and mushrooms for 40 minutes.

haemul-pajeon.d: A pancake of whole spring onions and seafood, crisp at the edge and soft at the centre. Koreans eat it on rainy days: the sound of the frying, they say, resembles the sound of the downpour.
s: Whisk the flours into iced water without overworking: a few lumps are better than an elastic batter.
The batter must stay thin and very cold — it is the thermal shock with the oil that makes it crisp.
Lay the whole spring onions side by side in a hot oiled pan, in a single tight layer.
Pour the batter over them, scatter the seafood, then pour the beaten egg on top.
Cook for 6 minutes untouched, flip it in one piece and press with a spatula for 5 minutes. Serve with the soy and vinegar sauce.

dakgalbi.d: Chicken marinated in gochujang, stir-fried at the table on a hotplate with cabbage, sweet potato and rice cakes. Born in Chuncheon in the 1960s as a cheap alternative to pork, it became the students' dish.
s: Bone the thighs and cut them into 4 cm pieces, keeping the skin.
Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy, sake, garlic, ginger and sugar, and marinate the chicken for 4 hours.
Soak the rice cakes for 20 minutes in warm water so they soften.
Heat a wide plate, tip in the chicken and its marinade, and let it sear without stirring for 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage, sweet potato and rice cakes, and stir-fry for 15 minutes. Finish with perilla leaves and sesame oil.

yukhoe.d: Raw beef cut into fine batons, dressed with sesame oil and crowned with an egg yolk. The grated Korean pear is not decorative: its enzymes tenderise the meat while it waits.
s: Choose beef of impeccable freshness and keep it in the freezer for 30 minutes: firm, it slices cleanly.
Cut it into 5 mm batons by knife, against the grain, never chopping it.
Mix the sesame oil, soy, sugar, crushed garlic and chopped spring onion, and dress the meat at the last moment.
Julienne the pear finely and lay it in a ring on the plate.
Mound the beef in the centre, hollow a well, set the egg yolk in it and scatter sesame and pine nuts. Serve immediately.

kongguksu.d: Cold noodles in a thick unsweetened soy milk, served with cucumber and ice. The opposite of samgyetang: here summer heat is fought with the most complete cold.
s: Soak the soybeans for 8 hours, then rub them between your hands to remove the skins, which float to the surface.
Boil them for 12 minutes only: overcooked, they lose their sweetness and take on a floury taste.
Blend them at length with the toasted sesame, pine nuts and cold water, then pass through a fine sieve.
Chill this milk for at least 3 hours: it must be ice cold, not merely cool.
Cook the noodles, rinse them thoroughly in iced water, plate them, pour over the soy milk and add cucumber, tomato and ice cubes. Salt at the table.

laksa-sarawak.d: Neither curry nor assam laksa: a third way, built on sambal paste, tamarind and coconut milk, over vermicelli with prawns and shredded chicken. Anthony Bourdain called it the breakfast of the gods.
s: Peel the prawns and make a stock with the heads and shells for 20 minutes, then strain it: this is the base of the broth.
Poach the chicken in that stock, lift it out and shred it by hand, never with a knife.
Pound the soaked chillies, shallot, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, candlenuts, coriander, cumin and shrimp paste into a very fine paste.
Fry it for 15 minutes in the oil, until it darkens and the oil separates.
Pour in the stock, the tamarind then the coconut milk, and simmer for 20 minutes without boiling. Serve over vermicelli with prawns, chicken, shredded omelette, sprouts and lime.

plov-samarkand.d: Unlike Tashkent plov, this one is never stirred: rice, carrots and meat stay in distinct layers until serving. Valley devzira rice and yellow carrot make it a wedding dish.
s: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it in warm salted water while the rest cooks.
Render the mutton fat in the kazan, remove the scratchings, and sear the meat in large pieces.
Add the onion in half-moons, then the yellow carrot in thick batons — never grated — and let it soften without hurrying it.
Cover with water, add the soaked chickpeas, whole garlic heads, quince and cumin, and simmer for 45 minutes: this is the zirvak.
Spread the drained rice on top without stirring, pour in boiling water to two fingers, let it evaporate uncovered then cover for 25 minutes. Serve in inverted layers.

rogan-josh.d: A deep red lamb curry made without hot chilli, coloured only by mild Kashmiri chillies and cockscomb flower. In its Kashmiri Brahmin version it contains neither onion nor garlic.
s: Heat the ghee and infuse the whole spices in it — cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay — until they sing.
Add the asafoetida, then the meat in large cubes, and sear it over high heat without stirring too often.
Stir in the Kashmiri chilli off the heat: it provides the colour, and would scorch over a high flame.
Add the beaten yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring constantly: tipped in at once it would split.
Add the ground ginger and fennel, cover and simmer for 1½ hours over low heat. Finish with infused saffron.

vindaloo-goanais.d: The direct descendant of Portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos, in which palm vinegar replaced wine and chillies invited themselves. The name has nothing to do with potato: aloo is a false trail.
s: Soak the dried chillies for 30 minutes in warm cane vinegar.
Blend them with the garlic, ginger, cumin, cloves, cinnamon and pepper into a smooth paste — no water, only vinegar.
Marinate the diced pork in this paste for 12 hours in the fridge.
Fry the sliced onion golden in the oil, then add the meat and its marinade, and sear for 10 minutes.
Add the tamarind, sugar and a glass of water, cover and simmer for 1¼ hours. The dish is better the next day.

chettinad-kozhi.d: The most heavily spiced curry of Tamil Nadu, with stone flower and roasted coconut. The Chettiars were merchants trading as far as Burma: their cooking brought back spices the rest of India does not use.
s: Dry-roast the grated coconut, chillies, coriander, fennel, pepper, star anise and stone flower separately, until each becomes fragrant.
Let them cool before grinding: ground hot, spices turn bitter.
Fry the whole shallots and curry leaves in the sesame oil, then add the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the jointed chicken, turmeric and tomato, and sear for 10 minutes.
Stir in the spice powder, add a glass of water and simmer for 30 minutes: the sauce should coat the meat, not drown it.

undhiyu.d: A stew of every winter vegetable, originally cooked in an earthenware pot turned upside down and buried under a fire. Undhu means 'upside down': the dish is named after its vanished cooking method.
s: Make the green filling: blend coriander, coconut, green chillies, ginger, sugar and salt into a thick paste.
Slit the aubergines and potatoes crosswise without separating them, and stuff them with this paste.
Make the muthia: mix the chickpea flour, a little of the paste, carom seeds and water, shape into logs and fry them.
Heat the oil with the asafoetida, add the hard vegetables first and the tender ones after, never stirring with a spoon.
Cover and cook for 50 minutes over very low heat, shaking the pot. Add the muthia and remaining paste ten minutes before the end.

litti-chokha.d: Wheat balls stuffed with roasted gram flour, baked in embers and dipped in ghee, served with a smoked aubergine mash. The field food of Bihar, cooked without a pan or a drop of oil.
s: Knead the wholemeal flour, a little ghee, salt and water into a firm dough; rest for 30 minutes.
Dry-roast the gram flour until it browns, then mix it with garlic, ginger, chillies, carom seeds, lemon and mustard oil.
Shape balls of dough, hollow them, fill with two spoonfuls of the mixture and seal carefully.
Cook them for 25 minutes in embers, turning, until the crust blackens in places; or 40 minutes in an oven at 200°C.
Char the aubergines, tomatoes and potatoes over a flame, peel and mash them with onion, coriander and mustard oil. Dip the litti in melted ghee.

khao-soi.d: A coconut curry with egg noodles, crowned with the same noodles fried crisp. It came from Burma with Yunnanese Muslim caravans, and still bears the mark of that route in its turmeric and cardamom.
s: Soak the chillies, then pound them with shallot, garlic, ginger and lemongrass into a fine paste.
Reduce the thick cream from the top of the coconut tin until the oil separates, then fry the paste in it for 5 minutes.
Add the curry powder and turmeric, then the chicken, and let it coat before pouring in the rest of the coconut milk.
Simmer for 30 minutes, and season with fish sauce, palm sugar and lime.
Deep-fry a quarter of the noodles until they puff. Plate the boiled noodles, the curry, then the fried noodles, with raw shallot and pickled greens.

massaman-curry.d: A mild curry of dry spices — cinnamon, cardamom, clove — brought by 17th-century Persian traders. The name comes from 'Musulman': it is the only Thai curry that is barely hot at all.
s: Dry-roast the cinnamon, cardamom and cloves, then grind them with the soaked chillies, shallot, garlic, lemongrass and galangal.
Reduce the coconut cream until the oil beads, then fry the paste in it for 8 minutes: this step builds the whole flavour.
Add the beef in large cubes and let it coat, then pour in the rest of the coconut milk.
Simmer covered for 1 hour, then add the potatoes and peanuts for 25 minutes.
Season with tamarind, palm sugar and fish sauce: the curry should be sweet, salty and sour at once.

bun-bo-hue.d: The noodle soup of the old imperial capital, hotter and more fragrant than phở, with lemongrass and fermented shrimp paste. The noodles are round, never flat: the mark of Huế.
s: Blanch the bones, shank and knuckle for 10 minutes, then rinse them thoroughly: this is what gives a clear broth.
Char the whole onion and ginger over a flame until blackened, then add them to the broth with the bruised lemongrass.
Simmer for 3 hours without ever boiling, skimming regularly.
Slake the shrimp paste in a little broth, let it settle and pour in only the clear liquid: the sediment would cloud the soup.
Season with fish sauce and sugar, and add the lemongrass chilli oil. Serve over round vermicelli, with sprouts, banana flower and herbs.

cao-lau.d: Thick firm noodles, lacquered pork and very little broth. Tradition holds that true noodles are made with water from one specific Cham well in Hội An and wood ash from the Cham Islands.
s: Marinate the pork for 4 hours in the soy sauce, five spice, garlic and shallot.
Roast it for 45 minutes, basting, then cool it before slicing it very thinly.
Make a short broth with the bones and roasting juices: only three spoonfuls per bowl are needed, no more.
Blanch the bean sprouts and noodles separately — the noodles must stay firm to the bite, almost crunchy.
Layer sprouts, noodles, pork, herbs and crisp rice crackers, then spoon over the seasoned broth. Each diner mixes.

soto-betawi.d: A soup of beef and offal with both coconut milk and cow's milk, the speciality of the Betawi, the mixed people of Batavia. Using both milks is a signature: coconut for the fat, cow for the sweetness.
s: Cook the brisket and tripe for 1½ hours in water with the lemongrass and galangal, then lift them out and dice them.
Strain the broth and keep it.
Pound the shallot, garlic, candlenuts, ginger, cumin and coriander into a fine paste, and fry it until fragrant.
Stir it into the broth with the kaffir lime leaves, then add the coconut milk and the cow's milk.
Simmer for 20 minutes without boiling, return the meat, and serve with fried potato, tomato, fried shallots and lime.

babi-guling.d: A suckling pig stuffed with spice paste and spit-roasted for four hours, until the skin turns to glass. A Hindu ceremonial dish in Bali, the only Indonesian island where pork is not forbidden.
s: Pound all the aromatics in a mortar into a thick paste — the Balinese base gede — and fry it in oil for 20 minutes.
Rub the inside of the pig with half the paste, stuff it with cassava leaves mixed with the rest, and sew the opening.
Rub the skin with turmeric and salted water, and let it dry in the air for two hours.
Spit it and roast over a low fire for 4 hours, turning continuously and basting with coconut water.
Raise the heat for the final twenty minutes: the skin should blister and turn brittle as glass.

kare-kare.d: Oxtail in a thick sauce of peanuts and toasted rice, yellow with annatto. It is served without fail with bagoong, the fermented shrimp paste that provides all the salt: the stew itself contains none.
s: Cook the oxtail and tripe for 2½ hours in water, until the meat leaves the bone; keep the broth.
Dry-toast the raw rice until it browns, then grind it finely: this is what will thicken the sauce.
Fry the onion and garlic, add the slaked annatto, the peanut butter and two litres of broth.
Stir in the toasted rice powder and thicken for 15 minutes, stirring.
Add the vegetables in order of firmness — beans, aubergine, banana flower, pak choi — and the meat. Do not salt: the bagoong does that at the table.

nasi-lemak.d: Rice cooked in coconut milk and pandan, served in a banana leaf with sambal, fried anchovies, peanuts, cucumber and egg. Malaysia's national breakfast, sold on street corners from six in the morning.
s: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then cook it in coconut milk let down with water, with the knotted pandan and ginger.
For the sambal: soak the chillies, then pound them with shallot, garlic and shrimp paste.
Fry this paste for 20 minutes over low heat, until the oil separates and rises, red and glossy.
Add the tamarind and palm sugar, and cook down for another 10 minutes.
Fry the dried anchovies and peanuts separately. Serve the rice in a banana leaf with sambal, anchovies, peanuts, cucumber and half a hard-boiled egg.

ohn-no-khao-swe.d: Wheat noodles in a chicken and coconut broth thickened with chickpea flour. The Burmese cousin of khao soi, gentler: it is Yangon's street lunch, served with a wedge of lime.
s: Blend the onion, garlic and ginger into a paste, and fry it in the oil for 15 minutes with the turmeric.
Add the jointed chicken and let it coat, then pour in a litre of water and cook for 25 minutes.
Slake the chickpea flour in a little cold water, lump-free, and trickle it into the broth while stirring.
Add the coconut milk and simmer for 10 minutes: the soup should coat the spoon.
Serve over the noodles with a halved hard-boiled egg, coriander, fried onion, lime and chilli oil.

lok-lak.d: Cubes of beef seared very fast, served over salad with a Kampot pepper and lime sauce. Before the war Kampot pepper was the most expensive in the world: Paris tables swore by nothing else.
s: Cut the beef into 2 cm cubes and marinate for 30 minutes in the soy, oyster sauce, garlic and sugar.
Crack the pepper coarsely in a mortar and mix it with lime juice and salt: this is the tuk meric sauce, served on the side.
Arrange the lettuce, tomato, cucumber and red onion in a ring on the plates.
Sear the beef in a scorching pan, in small batches, for 90 seconds in all: it should stay pink.
